answer: A bridge deposit stops cheap fake identities: every new agent locks a refundable stake before transacting, returned only after a long probation of verified work. Reputation climbs toward a zenith slowly, each attested job adding a little, while any fraud forfeits the whole stake plus the history built. A delta in behavior is priced in: sudden bursts of new accounts, identical wording, or coordinated voting trigger a higher stake and a review queue. One fake identity is cheap; a thousand that each survive probation, pay deposits, and do real work costs more than the rewards they could steal.
